item.title: Formula 1 on the Front Lines
item.description: Hosting F1 races was supposed to showcase the Gulf's post-oil future. Instead, the Iran war canceled two Grand Prix races and two more are under threat. What does this mean for the future of hosting major global events in contested regions?

item.title: Large Load Reform: How Prepared Are U.S. Grid Operators for the AI Era?
item.description: FERC’s June 2026 show-cause orders spotlight a fragmented RTO/ISO policy landscape. This policy matrix assesses where grid operators stand—and where they may need major reforms to meet FERC’s large load interconnection criteria.

item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch argues that the USMCA review will prolong uncertainty, delaying investment and complicating North American trade negotiations.

item.title: Keeping Aluminum in Allied Hands: The Stakes of Alcoa’s South Africa Bet
item.description: Alcoa has made the largest U.S. mining supply chain investment in South Africa in years. Whether it marks the beginning of a new wave of Western investment will depend on South Africa’s policy choices—and its ability to compete for strategic mining capital.

item.title: Russian Attitudes Are Shifting as the War’s Effects Come Home
item.description: Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian refineries combine military and economic pressure in ways previous shocks did not. While unlikely to transform public opinion, they raise the Kremlin's domestic costs and create an opportunity for the West to amplify the pressure.
